entry_points.name: delete_account
entry_points.note: HTTP route accounts/<int:pk>/delete/ calls Account.delete() on the instance.

entry_points.name: Account
entry_points.note: Account is registered in the Django admin, which offers the built-in delete action.

stores.name: accounts_account

fields.name: avatar
fields.note: Image field whose stored path is built under account/avatars/; the file itself is recorded as the separate store account.avatar.

erasure.note: The route resolves the Account and calls delete() on it, which removes the row.

stores.note: Table holding the account holder's name, email, avatar reference and join date.

stores.name: accounts_address

erasure.note: The foreign key to Account uses on_delete=models.CASCADE, so Django's collector deletes the address rows when the account row goes.

stores.note: Postal address rows linked to an account by foreign key.

stores.name: accounts_comment

fields.name: body
fields.note: Free text field a person types into; the schema does not constrain its contents.

erasure.note: The foreign key uses on_delete=models.DB_CASCADE, so the database removes the comment rows and no Django delete signal is emitted for them.

stores.note: Comment rows linked to an account by foreign key.

stores.name: account.avatar

fields.name: avatar
fields.note: The uploaded file stored under account/avatars/ is the image of the account holder.

erasure.note: A post_delete receiver registered for Account calls avatar.delete(save=False), and accounts/apps.py imports the signals module in ready() so the receiver is connected.

stores.note: Files uploaded through the Account.avatar image field.
